science.title: Prioritising emotional experience in pocket parks: towards human-centred design through Kano-based needs assessment
science.description: As a key component of sustainable urban planning, the emotional design of pocket parks warrants further investigation. Drawing on case studies of four typical pocket parks in Shanghai and 400 valid questionnaire responses, this study developed emotional need indicators based on emotional design theory and combined the Kano model, Better–Worse coefficients, and non-parametric tests to classify and prioritise users’ emotional needs and examine differences across user groups. The results show that Must-be qualities, such as Safety and Security Assurance, establish the baseline conditions for use; One-dimensional qualities, such as Environmental Restorativeness, have a strong capacity to enhance satisfaction; and Attractive qualities, such as Social Interaction, foster deeper emotional experiences. Qualities such as Accessibility of Digital Services and Biodiversity were classified as Indifferent. Based on these needs priorities, this study proposes emotional design strategies that prioritise securing Must-be qualities, focus on developing One-dimensional qualities, and moderately expand Attractive qualities. The findings provide context-specific guidance for the design and renewal of pocket parks in Shanghai and other comparable high-density built environments, while offering empirical insights into the shift of public-space design from a function-oriented approach towards a human-centred and emotion-oriented approach.

science.title: Efficient real-time vehicle tracking via lightweight YOLO and DeepSORT integration
science.description: Detecting and tracking vehicles ahead during driving is a critical technology for ensuring driving safety and enhancing the driving experience. However, traditional detection and tracking models often suffer from high computational intensity and large parameter sizes, making them unsuitable for resource-constrained mobile devices. This paper introduces a lightweight vehicle tracking model that integrates YOLO and DeepSORT. By incorporating GhostConv and C3GhostV2 modules into the backbone and neck networks of YOLO, we enhance detection accuracy while reducing model size. The Focal-EIoU function is utilized to improve the recognition of small, distant target vehicles. Additionally, ShuffleNetV2 replaces DeepSORT’s feature extraction network, further reducing model parameters. Experimental results demonstrate that among the latest models in the YOLO series, YOLOv5 offers more stable and accurate performance, making it a more suitable baseline for vehicle detection and tracking tasks. Based on this foundation, experimental results show that, compared to the baseline model implemented using the Ultralytics framework, the proposed model reduces GFLOPs by 37.1%, decreases the number of parameters by 34.5%, and achieves mAP@0.5 by 0.3%. The overall model size is only 13.62 MB, 44.8% smaller than the original. Validated on the SODA10M dataset, the model exhibits improved detection accuracy and maintains performance compared to other models, making it suitable for deployment on mobile devices during vehicle driving.
